Flavia, my director asked me a simple question. How has your program changed?
It has evolved a lot. When I started, we had three regions. Since then, the number has doubled.
Impressive. Has the growth been fast?
Not fast, but steady. So far, we have trained more than two thousand families.
And have buyers noticed the change?
Yes. That is the biggest change: recognition. Ten years ago, nobody asked for the label. Now buyers ask for it.
Good. So what is the challenge for the next decade?
To keep the momentum and make the program sustainable.

Hello, Flavia. This is Giorgio, from Bologna. Before our call next week, I have three questions for my report. First, how many producers have joined the program since the pilot started? Second, have your exports grown? My director wants one number, so please send me the percentage. And third, what has changed for the families? I would like one short story, if possible. You can send everything by email on Friday. Thank you, and talk soon.

When I started this job, ten years ago, the program had three regions and a very small team. Every meeting began with the same question: what is a geographic indication? Since then, a lot has changed. The number of regions has doubled, and we have trained more than two thousand families. The growth has not been fast, but it has been steady, and I think that is better. Our biggest milestone came in 2021, when a group of coffee producers sold their first container to Europe. So far, the program has been a success. Now our challenge is different. We need to make it sustainable, so it can continue for the next decade.

First, I say where we started ten years ago. Then, I say what has changed since then. Next, I give one number that has grown. After that, I say what we have achieved so far. Finally, I say what the next challenge is.
